Increases for 住友不動産, 住友林業 and 日本電気 are attributed to stock splits (footnote 4); NEC is also described as partly sold, so its net change is uncertain. policy_points: Shares are held for business purposes (transactions, financing, alliances) when judged to enhance medium- to long-term corporate value.
The board reviews each holding regularly against purpose, benefits and risks versus cost of capital, and non-economic contributions to value.
Shares judged unnecessary are sold; this year 4 issues were fully sold and 5 partially sold.
In March 2026 the board confirmed all holdings are necessary and will examine further reduction in light of requests to reduce cross-shareholdings.
Voting policy for held shares is not stated.
cross_holdings.policy_summary: The company holds shares only for business purposes when judged to enhance medium- to long-term corporate value. The board reviews each holding regularly against purpose, benefits and risks versus cost of capital, and non-economic value contribution, selling shares deemed unnecessary. It confirmed all holdings are necessary and will pursue further reduction.

exec_pay.notes: The 取締役 split (245 fixed / 179 performance / 41 stock, 6 people) was read from a flattened table string; the components sum to 465 against a printed total of 464, likely rounding. Individuals are those with consolidated pay of 100 million yen or more; Kajiya's components (53/41/9) sum to 103 against a printed 102. Monthly pay and bonus are reported together for the 監査役 and 社外 rows, which show fixed pay only.
policy_points: Target mix for executive directors (excluding outside directors): monthly pay 50%, bonus 40%, restricted stock 10%.
Bonus = base amount by rank × achievement coefficients for business profit (60%), ROE, GHG emissions reduction, CDP rating and female manager ratio (10% each), using 2024-26 medium-term targets.
Restricted stock is granted after the AGM and stays transfer-restricted until the holder leaves all director and executive officer posts; shares can be forfeited for violations.

A nomination and compensation committee, majority independent outside directors, decides individual pay and may cut or withhold pay if group performance sharply worsens or a director seriously damages corporate value.
Outside directors receive monthly pay only; the board's 2026 pay policy was approved on 30 March 2026.
exec_pay.policy_summary: Executive director pay: fixed monthly salary, performance bonus (business profit 60%; ROE, GHG cuts, CDP rating, female manager ratio 10% each) and restricted stock; outside directors get monthly pay only.

exec_pay.notes: The table lists 173 million yen total for the 6 non-outside directors, but fixed plus performance pay sums to 172 million, which looks like rounding in the source. The 35 million yen non-cash figure is the performance-linked stock compensation, per the footnote. No retirement benefits were paid. No individual's consolidated total reached 100 million yen, so no individuals are named. Shareholder-approved caps: 400 million yen per year for non-outside directors (50 million yen for outside directors), and 100 million yen per year for restricted stock.
policy_points: Mix: CEO 40% fixed and 60% performance-linked; other directors 50% fixed and 50% performance-linked. Performance-linked pay splits into bonus (CEO 45%, other directors 35%) and stock (15%).
Bonus metrics: consolidated sales, operating profit and ROE (financial and non-financial targets), with relative TSR weighted at 10%. Results are compared with targets and prior-year actuals.
Restricted stock: annual grant sized as a fixed share of individual annual pay, priced at the prior-day close, with transfer restrictions until the director leaves the board; granted in July.

Governance: a remuneration committee chaired by an outside director advises the board. The board delegates individual pay decisions to the Chairman and the President within the shareholder-approved caps.
Outside directors receive fixed pay only, reflecting their oversight role.
exec_pay.policy_summary: Pay for non-outside directors is fixed plus performance-linked bonus (tied to operating profit, sales, ROE, sustainability metrics and relative TSR) and restricted stock; outside directors receive fixed pay only.

Performance bonus: a 50–150% multiplier applied to a role-based standard amount, linked to consolidated operating profit and ROE, paid after fiscal year-end.

Performance stock: points granted by role each year over three-year periods; shares delivered on retirement, with a 50–150% multiplier on targets (initial period: operating profit growth, TSR, external-rating non-financial metrics) and part paid in cash equivalent.
Approved at the June 2026 AGM: up to ¥600m and 894,000 points over three years (1 point = 1 share) for eligible directors.
Nomination and Remuneration Advisory Committee, led by outside directors, reviews pay; the CEO sets individual amounts within board policy and must give maximum weight to the committee's advice.
Audit committee and outside directors receive base pay only, a monthly fixed amount set by role, tenure, peer benchmarks, company performance and employee pay levels.
exec_pay.policy_summary: Executive director pay is split 50:25:25 across base salary, performance bonus (consolidated operating profit and ROE) and three-year performance stock tied to operating profit growth, TSR and non-financial metrics; outside and audit directors get base pay only.
